title: Does Costco Cause Cancer? - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Alex Tabarrok highlights a takedown by Deric Tilson and Adam Stein showing that the Harvard T.H. Chan methodology linking nuclear power plant proximity to cancer produces even larger 'effects' for private universities and Costco, implying the nuclear-cancer papers capture a methodological artifact rather than real harm.

insights.claim: A Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health team led by Yazan Alwadi published a series of at least four papers (Environmental Health, Nature Communications, Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology, Environmental Epidemiology) claiming that living closer to nuclear power plants is associated with higher cancer incidence, cancer mortality and total mortality.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
entities: T.H. Chan School of Public Health
insights.so_what: A cluster of high-profile health papers can feed anti-nuclear sentiment and siting/licensing opposition even if methodologically weak.

insights.claim: Applying the same methodology used in the nuclear-cancer papers to other landmarks, Deric Tilson and Adam Stein find that living near a private four-year university is associated with a 15-fold larger increase in cancer mortality than living near a nuclear power plant.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Placebo tests show the reported nuclear effect is not specific to nuclear plants, undermining its use as evidence against nuclear power.
insights.quote: living near a private four-year university is associated with a 15-fold increase in cancer mortality when compared to living near a nuclear power plant
insights.locator: For instance, living near a private

insights.claim: Under the same method, Costco locations show the largest effect of any landmark tested, with over 2.2 million cancer deaths (more than 20% of US cancer deaths from 2000-2018) 'attributable' to Costco — a reductio showing the method is broken.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: An absurd result for a retailer signals the approach mechanically generates spurious associations with any widely distributed landmark.
insights.quote: Over 2.2 million cancer deaths can be attributed to Costco

insights.claim: The nuclear-cancer researchers picked nuclear plants because a story could be built around them and never checked what their methodology produced for other landmarks, so they could not know they were measuring the methodology itself.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
entities: T.H. Chan School of Public Health
insights.so_what: Narrative-first research without placebo checks is a generic source of false risk signals investors and policymakers should discount.
insights.quote: what they were actually capturing was the methodology itself

insights.claim: Tabarrok's bottom line: the number of deaths attributable to nuclear plants under this methodology is probably zero, while the number of bad papers it produced is at least four.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Reinforces the view that nuclear power's health risk to neighbors is not supported by this literature — relevant to nuclear restarts and new-build debates.
insights.quote: The attributable number of deaths from this methodology is probably zero, but the attributable number of bad papers is at least four.
